evidence: The homepage links directly to About, where the visible “Systems people can inhabit” section connects Open House to WOW List, Sunday Dinner/196, NYC Artist Coalition, and source-backed team memory; this satisfies the two-click requirement while the opening copy keeps technical project management, product operations, and implementation foregrounded.

The About page explicitly preserves the artistic, civic, technical, and social threshold without becoming an artist biography: Open House is presented as a bounded participatory experiment, followed by the professional sequence “observe relationships, model a system, prototype an interface, test it with people, and document enough for others to continue.”

At least three project continuities are concrete and public-safe: WOW List turns organizers’ own community vocabulary into distributed publishing tools; Sunday Dinner/196 turns hospitality, trust, onboarding, access, and follow-up into repeatable participation infrastructure; NYC Artist Coalition/FairRentNYC turns lived experience, meetings, public sources, questions, and decisions into recoverable coalition memory and action pathways.

The project traces explain the difference from conventional administration: people recognize relationships, participate through usable interfaces, preserve memory, influence revision, and carry work forward through documented handoffs.

Rendered desktop and mobile captures show the About lineage and Colophon as readable public surfaces. The Colophon further frames the portfolio as a selective, reviewable public edition with evidence, correction, permission, credit, and source-custody controls.

Collective contribution remains visible: WOW List is described as co-built; Sunday Dinner names community and co-organizer context; NYC Artist Coalition outcomes are explicitly collective; the Colophon states that projects are often collective and that case studies distinguish Jamie’s role from shared work.
gaps: The strongest lineage material begins below the initial About introduction, so mobile readers must scroll substantially before reaching the project comparison; this does not defeat the two-click criterion but slightly delays the threshold.

Open House receives only a concise public-source summary rather than its own captured case-study surface, so its evidentiary depth depends on the bounded source note and footnote context supplied in the packet.
safety_findings: No protected UCSC narrative evaluation, faculty testimonial, private correspondence, grade, or student record is quoted or projected in the reviewed surfaces.
The Colophon clearly states that named editorial perspectives are fictionalized simulations and do not constitute participation, quotation, endorsement, approval, or sign-off.

Sunday Dinner/196 withholds participant names, contacts, attendance histories, correspondence, addresses, access instructions, proposals, and unapproved images while using aggregate or reconstructed workflow evidence.
Collective-credit boundaries are consistently stated, and photographic captions identify courtesy or authorship without implying depicted-person endorsement.

Historical and emerging systems are bounded against inflated claims: WOW List’s relaunch is not presented as full restoration, source-backed team memory is not presented as completed client SaaS, and collective civic work is not converted into sole authorship or policy-impact claims.
recommendation: Pass PR-015. Preserve the current bounded Open House-to-current-practice threshold, collective-credit language, and protected-source exclusions; if revising, improve mobile wayfinding to the through-line without enlarging or personalizing protected historical material.

provenance.reviewMode: Fresh independent packet-only rendered-content holdout; no network, repository source, private records, parent directories, or sibling directories inspected
